articles.title: Cody Rhodes vs. Sami Zayn for WWE Undisputed Championship Announced Ahead of Crown Jewel
articles.summary: Sami Zayn will defend his WWE Undisputed Championship against Cody Rhodes on Monday's edition of WWE Raw, which will take place in San Diego's Pechanga Arena.
articles.body:
Sami Zayn will defend his WWE Undisputed Championship against Cody Rhodes on Monday's edition of WWE Raw, which will take place in San Diego's Pechanga Arena.

At this time, Zayn is scheduled to face World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel on Saturday, November 7 for the Crown Jewel Championships. However, Rhodes will face Reigns if he beats Zayn on Monday.

Zayn has held the belt since Sept. 11, when he beat CM Punk on SmackDown. He's defended the championship once in this reign against Kevin Owens on Sept. 18.

This is Zayn's second Undisputed WWE Championship reign (both were this year). The first began on June 27, when he beat Rhodes (then the champion) and Gunther in a triple threat match at WWE Night of Champions. He only held the belt for nine days, though, as CM Punk beat him on Raw to get the championship.

Cody Rhodes is currently in a feud with Randy Orton, but he'll temporarily set that aside for a shot at the belt. Rhodes is a three-time Universal champion and most notably won that championship at WrestleMania XL in April 2024 for his first-ever WWE world title.

Zayn and Rhodes have faced each other on television a few times this year, with the last match being on July 18, when CM Punk and Rhodes beat Zayn and Gunther in a tag team match at WWE Saturday Night's Main Event: NYC.

This match on Monday has far greater stakes, though, so we'll soon find out who will be facing Reigns on Nov. 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Parents speak out on The Ingraham Angle after girls forfeit race over biological male runner
articles.summary: Camas High School girls walked off a cross-country course after a transgender athlete switched from the boys' team to the girls' roster midseason.
articles.body: Roughly a dozen high school girls took their spots at the starting line of a Washington cross-country meet and walked off the course in protest. The Oct. 13 protest, reported by Fox News Digital's Jackson Thompson, at a Camas High School dual meet against Battle Ground followed a decision allowing a male athlete to switch from the boys' team to the girls' varsity roster midseason. On Sept. 5, the athlete finished 76th in an Oregon boys' junior varsity race. Just ten days later, that same runner was competing in the girls' division, as reported by OutKick's Matt Calkins. A CROSS COUNTRY RUNNER SWITCHED TO THE GIRLS TEAM MIDSEASON, PARENTS VOICE THEIR DISAPPROVAL AT MEET School officials were fine rubber-stamping the decision, but the young Camas runners weren't about to pretend it was a level playing field. They walked off the course. Parents Kevin and Sarah Burns appeared on "The Ingraham Angle" to explain why their daughter Holly and her teammates decided they had seen enough. "Well, we told her that they should do what they feel is best and that they feel is right. And they got the support from their teammates, and they decided to make a difference," Kevin Burns said. DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER "I think if only a couple of girls had walked off it, they would have lost some opportunities. And I don't think it would have mattered so much. But so many of them," he added. "And I want you to remember that several of the girls, such as the team, team captains, had quit before this. So there really was a lot more girls than you see in the video that were protesting this." When families questioned the runner's eligibility, the Camas School District said its hands were tied by state rules. WASHINGTON FAMILY REQUESTS SCOTUS INJUNCTION AFTER DAUGHTER WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE Officials explained that Washington law and high school athletic regulations require schools to let athletes compete in divisions matching their gender identity. Holly's father explained that the school's response effectively shut down the issue. WASHINGTON OFFICIALS CALL GIRL’S CLAIMED EMERGENCY ‘MANUFACTURED’ AFTER ALLEGED TRANS ATHLETE SEXUAL ASSAULT "The school sent us out a letter stating that, based on Washington law, it prohibits discrimination based on gender identity and expression," he said. When Ingraham summarized the letter as telling families they were out of luck, he agreed: "I guess it's okay to discriminate against actual gender." With athletic institutions and legacy sports figures largely silent, the burden of taking a stand fell on teenagers. I LOST A STATE CHAMPIONSHIP TO A BOY. I REFUSE TO LOSE MY VOICE Holly's mother addressed the emotional weight placed on young competitors who simply wanted to run. "They're children, they're, you know, they're 16 to 17-year-old girls that shouldn't have to deal with this at all, shouldn't even be on their radar," Sarah Burns said. "You know, they should just be able to go out there and race and have fun and not deal with this adult issue." The friction carried straight onto the sidelines during the meet. When the parents arrived with signs to support the runners, security attempted to remove them. WOMAN SAYS PUBLIC WAS FORCED TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA FORUM OVER HER 'SAVE GIRLS SPORTS' SHIRT "We've actually received a lot of support. I think that there's a big silent majority on this," Kevin Burns said. "I think people are afraid to speak out, but that was one of the reasons why we went down there and we held up signs." The couple stood their ground and refused to leave. NEW POLL SHOWS WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS ARE READY TO END BOYS COMPETING IN GIRLS' SPORTS "We got a lot of pushback showing up there. They said the signs weren't allowed. We had to leave. My wife Sarah was being very brave and did not care. And I don't think they had a legal reason to actually push us out," he recalled. "So we ended up actually staying there and holding our signs, and it gave the girls a boost of self-esteem. And we had a lot of parents coming up and saying, thank you for doing this. I was, I wanted to do this also. So this is kind of the start, I think." Her mother laid bare what is at stake: "I want to stand up for girls that need someone to stand up for them." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Kevin also pressed political leaders to take up the cause, arguing that defending female athletics bridges partisan divides. "This is a big issue that most Americans on both sides of the political aisle agree with. And I don't know why, party members, especially on the right, aren't grabbing this more and pushing it. "I know they have in the past, but this is such a winning issue," he said. "We have friends on both sides of the aisle that agree with the girls' rights to not have to compete against boys." The adults in charge won't do their jobs, so high school girls are doing it for them. Welcome to high school sports in 2026. articles.title: Hokato and Soman chase Asian Para Games gold
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Nagaland’s Hokato Hotozhe Sema heads into the Para Asian Games carrying both confidence and a touch of uncertainty. The world No.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Nagaland’s Hokato Hotozhe Sema heads into the Para Asian Games carrying both confidence and a touch of uncertainty. The world No. 2 shot putter in the F57 category was in good shape before an injury disrupted his preparations.“It was a minor injury near the hip region. I did the required exercises and it’s fine now. I am confident of achieving my personal best,” said the Paris Paralympics bronze medallist.While he may not have had the smoothest build-up to the Games, 2026 has still been a memorable year for Hokato. The 42-year-old became world No. 1 in his category and also set a national record with a massive throw of 15.21m at the Indian Open Para Athletics Championships in Bengaluru.But Hokato knows that if he is to stand atop the podium, he may have to get past a familiar face: Soman Rana.Ranked world No. 3, 43-year-old Soman Rana arrives at the Asian Para Games as the reigning Commonwealth Games champion and a two-time World Championships silver medallist, having finished runner-up in 2024 and 2025.The pair have trained together at the Army Paralympic Node in Pune since 2017 under coach Rakesh Rawat, developing both a strong friendship and a fierce rivalry. “We’re very close friends. We eat together, train together and spend a lot of time together. Our coordination is excellent,” said Soman, who suffered a mine blast injury while serving with the 2/8 Gorkha Rifles along the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir on Dec 1, 2006.For Hokato that friendship comes with an added competitive edge. “There is definitely a lot of competitiveness. We train together and help each other improve, but once competition starts, everyone wants to win,” he said.Rawat believes that rivalry has been one of the biggest reasons behind their development on the international stage.“They motivate each other a great deal,” Rawat said. “Training together gives them valuable experience. They are friends and support each other, but once competition begins, friendship takes a back seat and they become rivals. The one who performs best on the day wins.”The coach expects both throwers to be in contention for medals and insists there is little to separate them. “The rivalry between them has helped both improve. They are very closely matched. On the day, it could go either way,” he said.Soman agrees, although his Commonwealth Games gold is likely to provide an added boost. “The gold gave me a lot of confidence. But I’ve been in this sport for many years. My confidence was already there and winning the medal only strengthened it,” he said.While both athletes believe a podium finish is within reach, neither is willing to predict who will come out on top.For Hokato, however, a gold medal would carry special significance. Since winning bronze in Paris, the road has not been easy. His father passed away last Dec, while he has also been overseeing the construction of a house in his village of P. Vihoto in Nagaland and supporting his daughter, who recently began an MBA programme in Pune.On the field, injuries disrupted his season and forced him to miss the World Para Athletics Grand Prix in New Delhi. Yet, despite the setbacks, Hokato has remained focused on recovery and training.“Recovery is crucial. If you don’t recover properly, there’s no point competing. You can travel all that way and still return empty-handed,” he said.Now, he is eager to return to competition and renew his rivalry with Soman on one of para athletics’ biggest stages. articles.title: 11-time WWE World Champion announces retirement on live television
articles.summary: A multi-time WWE World Champion dropped a major announcement by revealing his retirement timeline on live television.
articles.body: A multi-time WWE World Champion dropped a major announcement by revealing his retirement timeline on live television. He is WWE Hall of Famer and current AEW star, Adam Copeland, formerly known as Edge. He has been a wrestling veteran for 25 years and came back from his first retirement in 2020. However, Cope has announced that he is set to put a permanent end to his wrestling career.Former WWE World Champion Adam Copeland announces retirementAdam Copeland competed in a singles match against former TNA star Josh Alexander on the October 14 episode of Dynamite/Collision. This was a Clockwork Carnage qualifying match, which the Rated-R Superstar won. After that, he grabbed the microphone and dropped a bombshell for the audience in attendance and millions watching at home. Cope announced that 2027 will be the final year he will remain active as an in-ring performer.Copeland said, "My face isn't on the poster on the teenagers' walls anymore. I'm aging out, and that's okay; it happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let you all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling. Hey, listen, I get it, I get it, it's time. But with all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship.”Adam Copeland returned to wrestling after his first retirement in 2011Adam Copeland was one of the top WWE superstars after his debut in 1999. In 2006, he won his first-ever WWE Championship. After that, he went on to become a marquee attraction for the company. However, Cope announced his retirement in 2011 due to serious neck injuries and retired as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion.He stayed away from the wrestling ring for nine years until his miraculous return at the 2020 Royal Rumble event. The Ultimate Opportunist remained with WWE until 2023, when his contract expired, and he chose to sign with rival promotion AEW. articles.summary: Another week of football is set to commence, but not for Cincinnati.
articles.body:
Another week of football is set to commence, but not for Cincinnati .

Bengals fans might notice this week's NFL schedule looks a little light (and they're not wrong). For those hoping to watch Joe Burrow and Co. , you'll have to wait another week.

Here's what to know about the Bengals schedule, including when they play next.

Cincinnati Bengals travel to Miami. Check out photos against Dolphins

When is the Bengals bye week? Do they play Sunday?

Unfortunately for Bengals fans, the team does not play this week.

Their bye week comes after defeating the winless Miami Dolphins 31-24 on Oct. 11. Other NFL teams on their bye week are the Detroit Lions (3-2), Miami Dolphin s (0-5) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0).

When do the Bengals play next? See upcoming opponent

The Bengals return from their bye week to face AFC North rival the Baltimore Ravens in Maryland on Sunday, Oct. 25.

The matchup comes after Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson sustained an ankle injury during the second half of Baltimore's Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans . He was ruled out for the team's "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 11.

As for his return, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson's status for Week 6 against the Cleveland Browns is unknown. So Bengals fans will have to wait and see if Jackson gears up in Week 7.

"To Lamar's credit, this dude's working his tail off to get back," Minter said. "He's in there all the time. Don't know the specifics of next week, but he'll be doing everything in his power to get back."

Former Bengal-turned-Raven Trey Hendrickson was also ruled out for Sunday night's game. He has not practiced since undergoing surgery for his finger injury during Week 4. It seems unlikely the linebacker will return for the Bengals.

articles.title: Federal court sides with Wrigley Field bullies | Strictly Legal
articles.summary: This is a weekly column for The Cincinnati Enquirer
articles.body:
Their fans routinely crowd into Great American Ballpark and root against the Reds;

I was prepared to add a fifth reason to the list when I read that the Cubs recently prevailed in a federal case in the Northern District of Illinois and obtained an injunction prohibiting a business located across the street from Wrigley Field from selling rooftop tickets to fans who want to watch Cubs games from that unique vantage point. I was all set to call them bullies, but as I reflected on the facts of the case, I must grudgingly admit that maybe the Cubs are right.

The defendant in the case is Wrigley View, a rooftop business located adjacent to Wrigley Field, offering views of the Chicago skyline, Lake Michigan, and Wrigley Field. The premises include stadium-style bleacher seating and a sky deck on the rooftop that can accommodate up to 200 guests.

From the seats at Wrigley View, customers can see into Wrigley Field over the barriers of the stadium. Wrigley View sells tickets to the rooftop on days there are games and events at Wrigley Field. It is only open for business on game days and days with other Wrigley Field events. The Wrigley View website includes a schedule of the Cubs' home games with hyperlinks to purchase tickets, comparing the Wrigley View experience to that of a ballgame at Wrigley Field.

The sole source of revenue for Wrigley View is selling tickets to its customers for admission to the rooftop, which includes unlimited ballpark-style concessions. Guests pay approximately $125 to $150 per person to purchase tickets. According to the court, Wrigley View made "a significant amount of gross ticket sale revenue in 2024 and the first half of 2025. In the spring of 2024, the Cubs installed four semi-transparent mesh screens obstructing the view from Wrigley View. Wrigley View continued to sell tickets even after the Cubs erected the screens.

The prior owner of Wrigley View had reached a settlement with the Cubs, which required Wrigley View to pay Plaintiff 17% of their Gross Revenues annually and 11% of Billboard Revenue for the duration of the Agreement. In exchange for making royalty payments as part of the Agreement, Wrigley View was granted rights to sell tickets to watch Cubs games from its rooftop, use certain Cubs trademarks, and advertise that they are endorsed by the Cubs. That ended on December 31, 2023. Before the Agreement expired, Wrigley View received a letter from the Cubs' outside counsel stating that when the Agreement term ended, Wrigley View would no longer have the rights to sell tickets and use Cubs trademarks. The letter added that "if you and the Cubs do not enter a new agreement by December 8, 2023, the Cubs will not engage in further discussions regarding calendar year 2024 and you will not be able to obtain any right or license from the Cubs for 2024."

After the Agreement expired, Wrigley View continued to operate its rooftop business and sell tickets to the experience of watching live Cubs ballgames. Upon receiving a copy of the complaint in this case, Wrigley View's owner informed its employees and its independent website developer that all marketing materials and the Wrigley View website had to be free of the Marks. Wrigley View reviewed and removed certain references to the Cubs, including changing its ticket names to simply "Chicago vs. [the opposing team]." However, following the filing of the complaint in this matter, the Wrigley View website still included a PDF brochure containing the Cubs logo. Wrigley View also continued to include the statement "Official Partner of the Cubs" in its marketing through 2025.

In ruling in the Cubs' favor, the court looked to a 1938 case where the court affirmed the Pittsburgh Pirates' right to shut down a radio station's broadcast of Pirates games. In that case, the radio station positioned observers at high vantage points to watch the ballgames over the fences and broadcast live play-by-play descriptions, despite lacking authorization to do so. The radio station sought to "justify its action on the ground that … its observers [were] stationed on its own property without trespassing on plaintiffs' property."

That defense didn't cut it in 1938, and it didn't work in 2026.

The court granted summary judgment in the Cubs' favor on claims of misappropriation, unjust enrichment, and trademark infringement. Once the court made those findings, it also granted a permanent injunction prohibiting Wrigley View from using the Cubs' marks and from selling tickets to view Cubs' games.

The court determined that customers were likely to be confused about the Cubs' relationship to Wrigley View. To support its case, the Cubs introduced reviews of the Wrigley View experience that included comments that its staff was "very rude and not accommodating," that the business will "rip you off," and that the business did not adhere to the terms of its customer contract. To the extent those customers would associate Wrigley View with the Cubs, the court concluded that Wrigley View's conduct "poses unmistakable peril to [the Cubs'] goodwill."

Wrigley View is admittedly David to the Cubs' Goliath. But their conduct here made it easier for the court to hand this one to the Cubbies.

Jack Greiner is a Cincinnati attorney. He represents Enquirer Media in First Amendment and media issues. He can be reached at greinerjack46@gmail.com .

articles.title: Yeboah scores 16th goal this season for Minnesota in 2-2 tie with Rapids
articles.summary: (AP) — Kelvin Yeboah scored his career-high 16th goal this season Wednesday night for Minnesota United in a 2-2 tie with the Colorado Rapids. Sayed Abu Farki...
articles.body:
COMMERCE CITY, Colo. (AP) — Kelvin Yeboah scored his career-high 16th goal this season Wednesday night for Minnesota United in a 2-2 tie with the Colorado Rapids.

Sayed Abu Farki subbed on for Keegan Rosenberry in the 60th minute, was shown a straight red card in the 68th and Colorado played a man down the rest of the way.

An own goal by Colorado's Loïc Williams capped the scoring in the 83rd. Hansen left his line and Yeboah played a low ball in front of the net where Williams misplayed a left-foot clearance that, as he fell to the ground, bounced up and deflected off his left thigh into the net.

Yeboah stole a pass in the attacking third, raced to the center of the area and beat goalkeeper Nico Hansen with a rolling shot in the 52nd minute that made it 1-1. The 26-year-old has at least one goal contribution in nine consecutive games and has eight goals and three assists in that span.

Darren Yapi redirected a volley , off an arcing cross played into the area by Rosenberry, into the net to open the scoring in first-half stoppage time and Georgi Minoungou scored from point-blank range into a wide-open net to give the Rapids (11-13-5) a 2-1 lead in the 74th minute.

Minnesota (7-12-10) is winless, with five losses, in its last eight games.

articles.body:
Temperance Bedford football coach Dave Mifsud asked his players an honest question after they beat Ann Arbor Huron in Week 7.

"If I told you back in March when I become your coach that we'd be 7-0, would you have believed me?"

Mifsud left Woodhaven last offseason to take over Bedford, just a two-mile drive from his house compared to the 40 miles north he used to travel to Brownstown.

The downside? He was leaving his established program for one that hadn't finished better than .500 in the previous three seasons.

Building something new would take sweat equity from his staff and players. And maybe it would be a while before Bedford started winning consistently.

Bedford (7-0, 5-0) is undefeated through seven weeks for the first time since 2013 and now has a chance to win the Southeastern Conference Red Division title when it hosts Saline (7-0, 5-0) in its conference finale Friday, Oct. 16.

"It's a first-year coach with a first-year system and we are getting better all the time, and I feel great about where we are right now," Mifsud said. "But we can't be satisfied. We've got to keep working. I think this team has a lot of potential and we're still growing and still learning."

A measuring-stick game against a juggernaut like Saline should tell Mifsud just how far his team has come.

Bedford is coming off a dominant performance at Huron, where quarterback Luke Whetstone and receiver Jaxson Lestock connected for two TD passes in the first half before running back Masyn Moran took over in the second.

Moran finished with 98 yards and a TD, including late runs of 19, 12 and 10 yards to help seal the 35-0 victory.

Linebacker Everett Wingate also dictated play defensively.

"We've got to play assignment football," Saline coach Kyle Short said. "We keep preaching to our defense to do their 1/11th, and we've got to be prepared for their buck-sweep, counter action run game while also being ready for their quarterback to throw the ball. Their running back is a monster, and you've got to tackle him low."

Saline has lots of talent, too, starting with sophomore quarterback Case Campbell , who has thrown for 1,183 yards and 21 TDs without an interception while completing nearly 70% of his passes. He's also rushed for three TDs.

Three-star senior Louis Esposito , a Michigan commit, anchors Saline's veteran offensive line. Running back Carson Cherry has rushed 78 times for 787 yards and 12 TDs, while Grand Valley State commit Cruz Hanson has caught 16 passes for 328 yards and eight TDs.

Western Michigan tight end commit Gabe Iadipaolo has added 259 receiving yards and four TDs.

Bedford will have its hands full against a Saline team averaging 49.9 points per game and known for making explosive plays.

"We're going in and playing one of the very best teams in the state, and we have the opportunity to compete for the league championship with them," Mifsud said. "We want to find out what we can do. We want to show up and give it our best and see what we can do. We want to compete and be on that level as Saline."

Clarkston (7-0, 4-0) at Harper Woods (6-1, 5-0), 7, Friday

One of the craziest finishes of 2025 was Harper Woods' 27-21 comeback victory over Clarkston, which went down as Clarkston's lone loss of the regular season.

Clarkston grabbed a commanding 21-0 lead before giving up 27 unanswered points to Harper Woods and quarterback Nate Rochelea , who threw for 240 yards and three TDs. Two went to Oregon commit Dakota Guerrant , the five-star receiver widely considered Michigan's top 2027 recruit by media outlets.

Rochelea has since graduated, but Guerrant and 35 other veterans are back, giving Harper Woods one of the deepest rosters in metro Detroit. For perspective, 12 of those veterans play on the offensive and defensive lines.

"Winning the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball will be critical to the success of both the offense and the defense," Clarkston coach Josh Pintar said. "Whoever does the best job in the trenches and whoever takes care of the ball the best will likely win this game."

Clarkston will counter with quarterback Alex Waszczenko , who has thrown for 670 yards and eight TDs with only two interceptions. Kiernan Riddle has carried the ball 42 times for 530 yards and five TDs, while Drew French has caught 10 passes for 230 yards and four TDs.

Hunter Kauth paces Clarkston's defense with 48 tackles, one sack and two interceptions.

"(We) have to be able to limit their explosive plays with their big playmakers," Pintar said. "Offensively, we need to take care of the ball and limit the negative plays, which is something we have been really good at lately."

Detroit Cass Tech (7-0, 5-0) vs. Detroit King (6-1, 4-1), 7, Friday, Ford Field

The Detroit Public School League capped ticket sales for the first meeting in Week 5 to keep things from getting too rowdy in the tight quarters at Detroit Cass Tech.

That won't be an issue during the rematch. Ford Field, home of the Detroit Lions, is once again hosting the PSL Final.

Detroit King is hoping for a different result after fumbling a 7-0 lead and allowing Cass Tech to score 20 unanswered points in a 20-7 loss.

Aside from Cass Tech's stellar defense, running back Julian Taylor was the star three weeks ago . He scored twice in the final seven minutes, including racing 48 yards for the go-ahead TD to clinch the victory.

Taylor iced the win with a 7-yard rushing TD with 1:49 left, spoiling any chance of a late King comeback.

The rematch should be just as close, only this time, the bigger venue and bigger crowd should crank up the intensity with a championship on the line.

Ecorse (7-0, 5-0) at Detroit Edison (6-1 5-0), 4, Friday

The numbers say this will be one of the closest games of the season, with football analytics blog Goosepoop favoring Ecorse by just half a point.

That says a lot about how far Ecorse has come since joining the Charter School Conference in 2024. It has gone from a middle-of-the-pack program to one of the league's best, with a chance to challenge defending Gold Division champion Detroit Edison for the title this week.

"In order for us to beat DEPSA, we will have to play a complete game in all three phases of football," Ecorse coach Larry Johnson said. "We have to make sure we don't beat ourselves because they are already a talented team with great coaching who doesn't need our help."

Quarterback Thomas Burgess II has thrown for 745 yards and seven TDs with just two interceptions to lead Ecorse's offense. Running backs Chrishaun Massey-Johnson and Rishon Langford-Smith have combined for 1,071 rushing yards and 19 TDs, while receiver Rakari Crocker has caught 16 passes for 312 yards and four TDs.

Langford-Smith also leads the defense with 40 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and an interception. Malik Putman has 33 tackles, 14 tackles for loss and four sacks, while Jaylen Banks has added 28 tackles and four sacks. Crocker has two interceptions.

"A few things that stand out about them is they are well-coached, big and athletic," Edison coach Chan Brock said. "They do a good job of mixing up run and pass and have been able to keep teams honest. They are able to hurt defenses with the run and pass."

Edison has plenty of firepower of its own. QB Myles Matlock has thrown for 1,100 yards and 15 TDs, while Jaivon Plowden has rushed for 840 yards and seven TDs. Kenji Wyche-El has caught 27 passes for 480 yards and three TDs, and Mekhi James-Davis has added 25 catches for 390 yards and four TDs.

Plowden also anchors the defense with 65 tackles and 12 tackles for loss. Ryan Thurmond has 87 tackles and 15 tackles for loss, while Karmelo Carlisle has 10 tackles for loss and two sacks. Andre Neal has four interceptions despite missing two games, and Jayden Taylor has picked off three passes.

"We will get lined up, play hard, smart and execute in moments and that should be enough to be successful in defending our Charter School championship," Brock said.

articles.title: Para cycling coach pulls out in protest; boccia added

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Para cycling chief coach Aditya Mehta on Wednesday withdrew from the Indian contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games in protest after eligible cyclists were denied selection. Arshad Shaik is now the lone cyclist to travel to Japan, with only a technician for support.Mehta, who has spent 13 years developing Indian para cycling, said he could not abandon athletes whose “hard-earned opportunities have been taken away”. Mehta will stay back in India while sending Shaik with technician Ramesh Pandi, along with the necessary equipment and technical guidance.“I need to stand by my other athletes, who have worked equally hard but have been denied their opportunity to compete at the Games,” Mehta told TOI, warning that the decision could jeopardise India’s Los Angeles Paralympic qualification prospects.He said India’s Asian rankings — seventh in the men’s category and fourth in the women’s — underline the importance of competing and accumulating points at crucial international events. The actual impact on qualification will depend on the applicable rules and final slot allocation.Boccia gets last-minute clearanceIn a late reprieve, the sports ministry approved two Boccia athletes, Sachin Chamaria and Anjali Devi, for the individual events after initially withholding clearance. Their inclusion takes India’s athlete strength to 168, with 112 men and 56 women competing across 11 disciplines. The overall contingent now stands at 281, including 113 officials.Soaring airfaresIndia’s para athletes have also been hit by delayed clearances, triggering a logistical scramble with direct flights to Nagoya no longer available and fares reportedly soaring to five times their usual levels.Athletes now are flying to Tokyo before undertaking a roughly four-hour bus journey to Nagoya, TOIhas learnt. articles.title: SMU vs. Virginia Preview: No. 24 Mustangs Face Rising Cavaliers in Dallas
articles.summary: The SMU Mustangs return to Gerald J. Ford Stadium on Saturday to host the Virginia Cavaliers in an important ACC matchup. Both teams enter the game at 4-2 ov...
articles.body:
The SMU Mustangs return to Gerald J. Ford Stadium on Saturday to host the Virginia Cavaliers in an important ACC matchup. Both teams enter the game at 4-2 overall and 2-1 in conference play, making this a valuable opportunity to strengthen their position in the ACC race.

SMU is ranked No. 24 nationally and has won two straight games, including a 25-16 victory over Boston College. Virginia also enters with momentum after rallying for a 28-25 comeback win over Syracuse.

Kickoff is scheduled for noon ET on The CW.

SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings will be one of the key players to watch Saturday.

Jennings has thrown for 1,588 yards this season and has continued to lead an offense capable of producing explosive plays. Head coach Rhett Lashlee has built the Mustangs around an aggressive offensive approach, and Jennings' ability to extend plays and make throws downfield remains central to the team's success.

Running back Kendrick Raphael provides another important option, giving SMU a rushing attack that can help take pressure off Jennings. The Mustangs will look to establish the run early while using their passing game to stretch Virginia's defense.

SMU has also been difficult to beat at home, winning seven straight games at Ford Stadium entering Saturday. The Mustangs will try to use that advantage to maintain their momentum.

Virginia quarterback Chandler Morris will lead the Cavaliers into Dallas as they attempt to earn their first road victory of the season.

Head coach Tony Elliott has Virginia playing competitive football, and last week's comeback against Syracuse demonstrated the team's resilience. The Cavaliers will need another complete performance against a ranked opponent.

Virginia must protect Morris, sustain drives and avoid giving SMU extra possessions. The Cavaliers will also need their defense to limit Jennings' explosive plays and force the Mustangs into difficult third-down situations.

The coaching matchup presents two different challenges. Lashlee wants SMU to play fast and create big offensive opportunities, while Elliott will look to keep Virginia disciplined and capitalize on mistakes.

SMU defeated Virginia 33-7 in their previous meeting in 2024, giving the Cavaliers additional motivation heading into Saturday's rematch.

With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, the matchup could have important implications for the ACC standings.

SMU will look to defend its home field and extend its winning streak, while Virginia hopes its recent comeback can translate into success on the road.

With Jennings leading the Mustangs and Morris directing the Cavaliers, Saturday's game should provide an important test for both programs as the conference season continues.

articles.title: Turnover woes continue as Christian Anderson Jr. makes his Hornets debut
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets fell to the Boston Celtics after committing 30 turnovers, despite an impressive debut from rookie Christian Anderson Jr.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets fell on the road to the Boston Celtics 114-93, their second loss of the preseason (1-2). Turnovers were a glaring issue once again, as Charlotte committed 30 giveaways, five more than the 25 they committed to open their preseason against the Brooklyn Nets .

That said, Charlotte had bright spots in other areas, including recent first-round pick Christian Anderson Jr., who made his team debut. Anderson Jr., the recent No. 18 overall pick from Texas Tech, scored 10 points in 21 minutes on 50% shooting from the field and 66% shooting from 3-point range. He also tallied one rebound, one assist and two steals.

In addition to Anderson Jr., it was Frenchman Tidjane Salaun who got the job done, tying Brandon Miller with a team-high 16 points to go along with one rebound and one assist. Salaun showcased an improved 3-point shot, converting on 4-of-8 attempts from beyond the arc.

With one more preseason matchup left to play (Oct. 16) against the Memphis Grizzlies , the Hornets will need to focus on taking care of the ball to put forth a more well-rounded effort.

articles.title: Alabama Will Miss Ryan Coleman-Williams Against Tennessee, But His Comeback Could Be Something Special
articles.summary: Neyland Stadium’s hostile environment awaits a shorthanded Crimson Tide offense as the star wideout’s injury leaves a leadership void that stats alone cannot...
articles.body:
There are certain players on a football team who bring so much more to the field than what shows up on a stat sheet. Players whose energy, leadership, determination, and passion are just as valuable as their athletic abilities. For the Alabama Crimson Tide, Ryan Coleman-Williams is undoubtedly one of those players.

And that is exactly why the news that Coleman-Williams will miss Saturday's rivalry matchup against Tennessee is such a disappointment.

I'm not going to sugarcoat it. This one hurts.

Not only because Alabama is preparing to walk into one of the most hostile environments in college football without its leading receiver, but because of how much Coleman-Williams means to this Alabama football team. He has worked incredibly hard to become one of the most important pieces of the Crimson Tide's offense, and there is absolutely no doubt that Alabama would love to have him on the field when the Third Saturday in October rolls around.

But as disappointing as this injury is, I genuinely believe something special could be waiting for Coleman-Williams on the other side of this setback.

And I wouldn't bet against him for a second.

Alabama's initial availability report on Wednesday officially listed Coleman-Williams as out for Saturday's matchup in Knoxville. The junior wide receiver has been dealing with a knee issue, along with a head injury sustained during Alabama's heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia. Head coach Kalen DeBoer indicated earlier this week that Coleman-Williams would likely be evaluated on a week-to-week basis after the Tennessee game.

For Alabama fans, the timing could hardly be worse.

Coming off an emotional loss to Georgia, the Crimson Tide desperately wants to get back in the win column and prove that its championship aspirations remain very much alive. Tennessee is not exactly the opponent you want to face when you're trying to regroup, especially on the road at Neyland Stadium. And when you're preparing for a rivalry game of this magnitude, you want every weapon available.

Coleman-Williams is not just another offensive weapon. He is one of the players who can completely change the trajectory of a football game with a single touch of the football. Through Alabama's first six games, he has recorded 23 receptions for 415 yards and four touchdowns. Those numbers tell part of the story, but they don't come close to capturing his complete impact on this offense.

There is something different about the way Coleman-Williams plays football.

He has that competitive fire that Alabama fans have come to appreciate over the years. He isn't afraid of the big moments, doesn't shy away from physicality, and has continued developing into the kind of player opposing defensive coordinators must account for every single week.

More importantly, he has become a player his teammates can depend on.

And that's what makes watching him deal with another setback so frustrating.

During Saturday night's matchup against Georgia, Coleman-Williams battled through adversity before ultimately leaving the game. He initially went down while attempting to make a play in the end zone, but returned to action. Later, after taking a hard hit, he was forced to leave again.

Watching a player who gives everything he has to his team suffer an injury is never easy. And considering the circumstances surrounding Alabama's loss to Georgia, the entire situation was even more difficult to stomach.

However, there is something DeBoer said earlier this week that really stood out to me.

When discussing Coleman-Williams, DeBoer talked about the things fans don't always see. The work players put in behind the scenes, the physical challenges they push through during the week, and the effort required just to be ready when Saturday arrives. He specifically praised Coleman-Williams for continuing to encourage his teammates and bring positive energy despite battling injuries himself.

And to me, that says everything about the kind of player Alabama has in Ryan Coleman-Williams.

Anybody can be excited when they're healthy, scoring touchdowns, and hearing 100,000 people cheering their name. But what about when things aren't going your way? What about when you're hurting, frustrated, and physically unable to contribute the way you want to?

And I believe Coleman-Williams is going to continue being a leader for Alabama, even if he's standing on the sidelines instead of lining up at wide receiver this Saturday.

Of course, Alabama's offense is going to have to adjust without him. Keelon Russell will need other receivers to step up, and offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb will have to find ways to keep this offense explosive despite losing one of its most reliable playmakers. But that's also part of what makes championship-caliber football teams special. Adversity creates opportunities, and sometimes the absence of one great player becomes an opportunity for another to establish himself.

Alabama has talented players throughout its offensive roster. Now it's time for some of them to show exactly what they're capable of doing. That doesn't mean replacing Coleman-Williams will be easy. Quite frankly, I don't think you can replace everything he brings to this team with one player. But Alabama can still win this football game. And I certainly hope the Crimson Tide gives Coleman-Williams something to celebrate while he focuses on getting healthy.

Which brings me to something else I feel strongly about.

I do not believe we have seen the best of Ryan Coleman-Williams this season. Not even close.

Obviously, nobody can guarantee when an injured player will return, especially when a head injury is involved. His health must come first, and Alabama's medical staff needs to ensure he is fully ready before clearing him to compete again. But assuming he is able to return this season, I genuinely believe Coleman-Williams has the potential to come back even stronger.

Why? Because of everything we've already seen from him.

This is a young man who has demonstrated incredible toughness, resilience, and a willingness to do whatever his team needs. He has earned his opportunities through hard work, and he has continued proving that he belongs among the most dangerous offensive weapons in the Southeastern Conference.

I don't see a competitor like that allowing one setback to define his season. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if this experience gives him even more motivation when he's finally cleared to return. Imagine Coleman-Williams stepping back onto the field later this season, healthy, hungry, and determined to make up for the opportunities he missed.

Imagine the impact he could have during the final stretch of Alabama's regular season, particularly if the Crimson Tide is fighting for an SEC Championship appearance and a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Those are the moments that can define a player's legacy. And considering how much he has already contributed to Alabama, I would absolutely love to see Coleman-Williams get that opportunity.

One of my favorite things about college football is watching young men respond to adversity. We spend so much time discussing statistics, rankings, recruiting stars, and championship expectations that we sometimes forget these are young men dealing with real physical and emotional challenges.

An injury doesn't just affect a player's ability to participate in a football game. It can be mentally exhausting, especially when you've spent countless hours preparing for moments like Saturday's rivalry matchup against Tennessee.

I can only imagine how disappointing it must be for Coleman-Williams to know he won't be out there battling alongside his teammates in Knoxville.

One missed game does not erase what he has accomplished, what he means to this team, or what he is capable of accomplishing before this season is over. Alabama fans have seen enough from Coleman-Williams to know what kind of competitor he is. And if there's one thing I know about competitors, it's that they don't need much additional motivation to prove themselves.

I expect Alabama to miss him tremendously against Tennessee. That's simply the reality of losing a player of his caliber. But I also expect the Crimson Tide to rally around him, compete with everything it has, and make sure this injury doesn't become an excuse for anything less than its best performance.

As for Coleman-Williams, I'm choosing to be optimistic.

Maybe his greatest performance of the season is still ahead of him. Maybe the most memorable touchdown, the biggest catch, or the defining moment of his 2026 campaign hasn't happened yet.

For now, I just want to see him healthy.

Football is important, especially here in Alabama, but the well-being of these young men will always matter more than the outcome of a game.

Still, I cannot help but believe that when Ryan Coleman-Williams is finally able to put that Crimson jersey back on and run onto the field, he's going to have a little extra fire in his heart. And if that happens, I feel sorry for the defensive backs who have to line up across from him.

Because something tells me Ryan Coleman-Williams isn't finished making headlines this season.

His story isn't over. And I have a feeling the best chapter might still be waiting to be written.

articles.title: WWE Legend Adam “Edge” Copeland Announces AEW Retirement
articles.summary: Wrestling legend Adam Copeland officially revealed that he will be retiring from the ring in 2027. Formerly known in WWE as Edge for decades, Copeland made t...
articles.body:
Wrestling legend Adam Copeland officially revealed that he will be retiring from the ring in 2027. Formerly known in WWE as Edge for decades, Copeland made the jump to AEW to wrestle under his real name. The epic tag team reunion of Copeland and Christian Cage showed him as a huge part of AEW's highly successful 2026 so far. Copeland returned after a short break tonight to defeat Josh Alexander.

The match saw Copeland advancing to a Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship at WrestleDream 2026. Copeland felt it was time to make the news public that he will be retiring with AEW at some point in 2027. AEW hopes that this will add higher stakes to the unique new match since Copeland now has a chance to win the world title.

Will Ospreay will defend the title against Copeland and six other wrestlers in a risky concept. Copeland's news has become the biggest AEW story of the night and the top news in wrestling. WWE witnessed Edge thriving as a top star for many years to become an all-time great. Copeland joined AEW for new opportunities and more creative freedom to help the younger promotion gain more momentum.

Which Month Will Adam Copeland Retire In?

Copeland only named the year 2027 when discussing his retirement and making it clear the end date is coming up closer. AEW has yet to reveal any locations for 2027 AEW PPVs beyond Dynasty in the United Kingdom for early February.

The retirement date of Copeland will likely be known when the PPV schedule gets fully announced. Tony Khan' s respect of the talent and wrestling history will make it a safe bet that AEW gets a Canada venue to host Copeland's final match. A hometown crowd treating Copeland with full respect is the right way to end his career.

Copeland could also consider another major market like New York since they are rumored to have a big event next year. All In 2027 will be the biggest show of the year to make that realistic. Multiple scenarios exist, but Copeland will likely retire at some point between All In during the summer and the end of the year.

Who Will Be Adam Copeland's Final Opponent?

One interesting factor now is seeing which matches get booked now that we know Copeland will have a retirement tour. WWE recently told a polarizing story of John Cena' s retirement tour featuring both beloved moments and criticized decisions.

Ospreay, Swerve Strickland , MJF, and Adam Page are four of AEW's top stars yet to have a program with Copeland. All these names make sense for matches in the final year since Copeland wanted to have dream matches against first-time opponents.

Christian Cage makes sense to be a big variable in this story as either a tag partner or opponent once more. Younger talents like Nick Wayne or Kyle Fletcher could be made into a bigger star from retiring Copeland. AEW has many options, but MJF would be the smartest bet based on the money such a match would draw.

articles.title: UC Bearcats entertain national semifinalist Illinois on home hardwood
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bearcats basketball hosts 2026 national semifinalist Illinois at Fifth Third Arena Oct. 17. Here's the scouting report
articles.body:
Some University of Cincinnati men's basketball history will be made Saturday, Oct. 17, even though it's an exhibition game.

Each previous matchup between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Illinois has taken place at a neutral site. This game at Fifth Third Arena is the first time one of the squads has stepped foot in the other's gym.

Illinois does so with a great deal of confidence, returning three starters from a team that played in the Final Four at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Illini lost to Connecticut 71-62 to end their season 28-9.

This is the first exhibition for Illinois, while UC and Ohio State did battle at the Lindner Tennis Center Oct. 7, with the Bearcats prevailing 79-68.

"To beat a team that went to the Round of 32 with some guys back, that's a pretty good sign," UC Bearcats coach Jerrod Calhoun said. "That's a pretty good win in your first game."

Cincinnati Bearcats basketball head coaches over past 80 years

3 keys for Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Illinois

1. Cincinnati Bearcats must avoid injuries

Myles Colvin stumbled out of bounds early in the game against Ohio State and left after playing just 2:41. UC coach Jerrod Calhoun said Colvin could have returned if needed, but was left out as a precaution. Colvin returned to practice two days later. Colvin started vs. Ohio State and is a veteran who averaged 11.6 points and 4.4 rebounds for Wake Forest last season, shooting 36% from the perimeter and 87% from the free-throw line. Colvin played against Illinois in 2024-25 while at Purdue.

2. Stop Illinois forwards in paint, perimeter

Illinois features a pair of talented forwards on the Preseason All-Big Ten Team: sophomore David Mirkovic and wing Andrej Stojakovic. Mirkovic averaged 13.3 points and eight rebounds as a freshman, while Stojakovic averaged 13.5 points and 4.5 rebounds and made the NCAA All-South Regional Team in their run to the Final Four. They are two of the five rotation players the Illini have back from last season's national semifinalists.

3. Cincinnati Bearcats fans must still remember exhibitions don't count

With two recent exhibition wins over Ohio State and a win over 2026 NCAA champion Michigan last season, Illinois presents a tough challenge, having been to last year's Final Four. The early KenPom rankings have them fourth in the country and ESPN gives them a preseason ranking of No. 3.

A win might help sell some Fifth Third Arena season tickets (and by the way, this exhibition was not included in your season ticket package ). But the NCAA Selection Committee doesn't factor in October results; otherwise, recent closed-scrimmage wins by Queens College over Florida State or USF over the Miami Hurricanes might matter more.

"This is a dangerous team; we can just fire on all cylinders," UC's Tylen Riley said post-Ohio State.

The most impressive takeaway from the opening game was UC took the lead with 5:11 to go at 64-62, then outscored Ohio State 15-6 the rest of the way. Wes Miller's teams weren't known for late-game comebacks.

Tip: 5 p.m., Oct. 17, Fifth Third Arena (12,012)

Series : Illinois leads 3-2 (non-exhibitions)

Stefan Vaaks (G, 6'7", 15.8 ppg at Providence)

Quentin Coleman (G, 6'4", 23.1 ppg as 5-star high school player)

Coach: J errod Calhoun, first year; 297-159 overall with five seasons in Division II and nine in Division I

Cincinnati Bearcats, Illinois Fighting Illini to watch

Stojakovic is a 22-year-old senior for Illinois who is the son of 13-year NBA veteran Peja Stojakovic and a contender to be a first-round pick himself. He surpassed 20 points eight times last season and had a high game of 30 against Maryland. It's his second season with Illinois. He previously played single seasons at Cal and Stanford.

After missing the Bahamas exhibitions with a hand injury, Tulsa transfer Tylen Riley didn't start, but played nearly 25 minutes in the Ohio State win, scoring 18 of his 23 points in the second half. Riley dished out three assists and had two steals in addition to getting to the free-throw line for 16 of UC's 32 shots from the stripe.

articles.summary: Cincinnati Bearcats basketball hosts 2026 national semifinalist Illinois at Fifth Third Arena Oct. 17. Here's the scouting report
articles.body:
Some University of Cincinnati men's basketball history will be made Saturday, Oct. 17, even though it's an exhibition game.

Each previous matchup between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Illinois has taken place at a neutral site. This game at Fifth Third Arena is the first time one of the squads has stepped foot in the other's gym.

Illinois does so with a great deal of confidence, returning three starters from a team that played in the Final Four at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Illini lost to Connecticut 71-62 to end their season 28-9.

This is the first exhibition for Illinois, while UC and Ohio State did battle at the Lindner Tennis Center Oct. 7, with the Bearcats prevailing 79-68.

"To beat a team that went to the Round of 32 with some guys back, that's a pretty good sign," UC Bearcats coach Jerrod Calhoun said. "That's a pretty good win in your first game."

Cincinnati Bearcats basketball head coaches over past 80 years

3 keys for Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Illinois

1. Cincinnati Bearcats must avoid injuries

Myles Colvin stumbled out of bounds early in the game against Ohio State and left after playing just 2:41. UC coach Jerrod Calhoun said Colvin could have returned if needed, but was left out as a precaution. Colvin returned to practice two days later. Colvin started vs. Ohio State and is a veteran who averaged 11.6 points and 4.4 rebounds for Wake Forest last season, shooting 36% from the perimeter and 87% from the free-throw line. Colvin played against Illinois in 2024-25 while at Purdue.

2. Stop Illinois forwards in paint, perimeter

Illinois features a pair of talented forwards on the Preseason All-Big Ten Team: sophomore David Mirkovic and wing Andrej Stojakovic. Mirkovic averaged 13.3 points and eight rebounds as a freshman, while Stojakovic averaged 13.5 points and 4.5 rebounds and made the NCAA All-South Regional Team in their run to the Final Four. They are two of the five rotation players the Illini have back from last season's national semifinalists.

3. Cincinnati Bearcats fans must still remember exhibitions don't count

With two recent exhibition wins over Ohio State and a win over 2026 NCAA champion Michigan last season, Illinois presents a tough challenge, having been to last year's Final Four. The early KenPom rankings have them fourth in the country and ESPN gives them a preseason ranking of No. 3.

A win might help sell some Fifth Third Arena season tickets (and by the way, this exhibition was not included in your season ticket package ). But the NCAA Selection Committee doesn't factor in October results; otherwise, recent closed-scrimmage wins by Queens College over Florida State or USF over the Miami Hurricanes might matter more.

"This is a dangerous team; we can just fire on all cylinders," UC's Tylen Riley said post-Ohio State.

The most impressive takeaway from the opening game was UC took the lead with 5:11 to go at 64-62, then outscored Ohio State 15-6 the rest of the way. Wes Miller's teams weren't known for late-game comebacks.

Tip: 5 p.m., Oct. 17, Fifth Third Arena (12,012)

Series : Illinois leads 3-2 (non-exhibitions)

Coach: J errod Calhoun, first year; 297-159 overall with five seasons in Division II and nine in Division I

Cincinnati Bearcats, Illinois Fighting Illini to watch

Stojakovic is a 22-year-old senior for Illinois who is the son of 13-year NBA veteran Peja Stojakovic and a contender to be a first-round pick himself. He surpassed 20 points eight times last season and had a high game of 30 against Maryland. It's his second season with Illinois. He previously played single seasons at Cal and Stanford.

After missing the Bahamas exhibitions with a hand injury, Tulsa transfer Tylen Riley didn't start, but played nearly 25 minutes in the Ohio State win, scoring 18 of his 23 points in the second half. Riley dished out three assists and had two steals in addition to getting to the free-throw line for 16 of UC's 32 shots from the stripe.

articles.title: Bold predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats Big 12 game at West Virginia
articles.summary: Here's how Cincinnati Bearcats football can get a Big 12 road win at West Virginia Oct. 17
articles.body:
Two teams that began undefeated will try to hit the brakes in the loss column Oct. 17 at noon at Milan Puskar Stadium in Morgantown. The Cincinnati Bearcats began 4-0 in September, but got punched in the mouth at Arizona 34-7 in their first game of October.

West Virginia started the second season of head coach Rich Rodriguez 2.0 at 3-0. Since then, they have lost three straight Big 12 games to Oklahoma State, Iowa State and that same Arizona team that beat UC. Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita and company outscored the Mountaineers 52-31 Oct. 10.

The Bearcats were thrashing teams in the run game until Arizona, which held them well below their average with just 74 yards. UC still is No. 12 among FBS schools, averaging 230.8 yards per game.

West Virginia has the second coming of "heyday" Mountaineer teams featuring running back Steve Slaton and quarterback Pat White, who averaged over 100 yards rushing each in three straight wins over the Bearcats in 2005, 2006 and 2007.

Current WVU quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. and running back Cam Cook have combined for 1,465 yards, making them the best tandem rushing threat in football. WVU averages 295.5 yards on the ground, behind only the service academies Army, Air Force and Navy.

"They're going fast," UC Bearcats head coach Scott Satterfield said. "Getting the calls from the sideline, making sure you're on the same page (is important). That's part of why they do go fast, to screw with the defensive call. That's another thing that's going to be a challenge."

Who will throw better, UC's JC French IV or WVU's Michael Hawkins Jr.?

In terms of completion percentage, Cincinnati Bearcats QB JC French IV is No. 20 in the nation, just shy of 70%. West Virginia's Hawkins is No. 128 of 129 at just over 52%. But in passing yards per completion, Hawkins leads the nation at 18.19 yards per reception, thanks to receiver DJ Epps, who leads the nation at 28.07 yards per reception and has four touchdown catches.

French is No. 96 at just over 11 yards per reception, and his deep threat, wide receiver JV Gibson, was shut out at Arizona.

"Their offense is really good and capable of scoring a lot of points," French said. "I think we have to score a lot of points as well. I think we're capable of that. I think it's going to be a high-scoring game and it's going to be fun."

How Cincinnati Bearcats have played in Morgantown

West Virginia leads the all-time series 18-3-1, with UC not winning in Morgantown since 2008, when Tony Pike hit Kazeem Alli for an overtime touchdown in a 26-23 victory. UC Bearcats defensive line coach Walter Stewart played in that game and in the following year's win in Nippert over the Mountaineers . UC's only other win in Morgantown came in 2003 when Chet Ervin hit five field goals and the Bearcats handed WVU's Rich Rodriguez his lone loss in the series. The Mountaineers are 9-2-1 in Morgantown vs. UC and 9-1 in Cincinnati.

3 bold predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats at West Virginia Mountaineers

Who has led Cincinnati Bearcats football over for past 80 years?

1. UC, WVU will both feature 100-yard rushers

The only game Jacksonville State transfer Cam Cook was held below 100 yards rushing was in a blowout against Tennessee-Martin when he was out of the game. Quarterback Hawkins was "held" to 96 yards vs. UT-Martin and 98 vs. Arizona, but passed the century mark in the other four games.

UC's Gi'Bran Payne has had three games of 100-plus yards and Cole Tabb has one. It's hard to imagine UC getting stuffed at the line of scrimmage the way they were against Arizona.

2. UC QB JC French IV will have to throw for over 200 yards

Outside of the Victory Bell win over Miami University and the Western Carolina game, UC's approach has been ultra-conservative. If you look at West Virginia's three losses, they were outpassed by a considerable margin. Oklahoma State threw for 389 yards, Iowa State for 312 and Arizona for 341.

French's high was 309 against the Miami's RedHawks. The numbers look like he'll need at least 200 here to avoid West Virginia crowding the line.

3. UC, WVU over/under is 63.5, but final score will be under

Even JC French has predicted a high-scoring game here, but if UC defensive coordinator Nate Woody can somehow keep the Mountaineers under 30, you would think UC has enough offensive firepower to win. West Virginia's season-low in scoring came in their opener, a 31-24 win over Coastal Carolina.

Though UC allowed 34 points to Arizona, those that stayed up to watch the game know it could have very easily been 10-10 at the half, which probably changes the complexion of the second half.

What West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said about Cincinnati Bearcats

In his remarks to West Virginia play-by-play veteran Tony Caridi this week, "Rich Rod" spoke of UC's preparation time between the Oct. 3 loss to Arizona and being able to watch West Virginia lose to Arizona Oct. 10, 52-31.

"You expect to see new things and inevitably you usually don't see a lot of new stuff because they usually just work on their fundamentals, which everybody wants a week for fundamentals," Rodriguez said. "But they do a lot of things formation-wise on special teams; I think they will do some new blitzes defensively and then from their offense, we've got to be ready for just about anything."

West Virginia averages 36 points per game, but gives up nearly 33. In their three straight Big 12 losses, they've given up 41 at home to Oklahoma State, 45 on the road at Iowa State and 52 at home to Arizona.

"We know what we're doing can be fixed, but it's got to get fixed in a hurry schematically and fundamentally," Rodriguez said.

Possession time has been an issue with UC and WVU, with both averaging about 29 minutes per contest. The Mountaineers had the ball nearly 36 minutes to Arizona's 24 last week, and they ran 104 plays to Arizona's 51. Obviously, the Wildcats made them pay.

"Last week, we probably had some more deep shots, but we didn't want to take them because we wanted to control the ball," Rodriguez said. "This week, we are going to have to have some patience."

Predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats at West Virginia Mountaineers

Enquirer prediction for Cincinnati Bearcats at West Virginia Mountaineers

The Enquirer has been right on every game thus far, but off on the final scores (as dramatically shown at Arizona). In the preseason, I picked this as a 23-17 UC win. That was well before the running exploits of Cook and Hawkins. No one has stopped their running game, but every team that's beaten them has won in passing yards.

Because I think this win is crucial to UC's success this season, with three Top 25s in a row coming up, I'll stick to the win prediction, but up the score by 10 points on each side for a 33-27 Bearcats win. As always, turnovers will be crucial, and the Bearcats had an extra week to prepare.

articles.title: NASCAR Truck Series Preview: Championship Battle Heats Up at Phoenix
articles.summary: The NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series heads to Phoenix Raceway this Friday for the Zero Carbon Bioethanol 150 Powered by POET, with the championship battle enter...
articles.body:
The NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series heads to Phoenix Raceway this Friday for the Zero Carbon Bioethanol 150 Powered by POET, with the championship battle entering another important stage of the postseason.

The 150-mile race is scheduled for October 16 at 7:30 p.m. ET, with coverage on FS2. The one-mile Arizona oval will host 150 laps as the remaining championship contenders look to gain valuable ground with the season moving closer to its conclusion.

One of the biggest storylines heading into Phoenix is Layne Riggs , who is coming off a dramatic victory at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

Riggs drove his No. 34 Ford for Front Row Motorsports to victory in the Ecosave 200, passing championship rival Kaden Honeycutt late in the race. The win added another major result to Riggs' season and gave him momentum heading into the next round.

After showing speed throughout the Charlotte race, Riggs will look to carry that performance into Phoenix. With the championship fight tightening, another strong finish could prove important as the postseason continues.

Honeycutt will also be a driver to watch after a strong performance at Charlotte. He led the most laps and won Stage 2 before Riggs made his late pass for the victory.

Despite missing out on the win, Honeycutt showed that he has the speed to compete at the front. His ability to maintain track position and execute during the closing laps will be important at Phoenix, where small mistakes can have major consequences.

Other championship contenders, including Chandler Smith and Gio Ruggiero, will be looking for opportunities to close the gap as the pressure increases.

Phoenix Raceway presents a different test from Charlotte's intermediate oval. The one-mile track features varying corner banking, making handling and tire management important throughout a long run.

Drivers will need to find a balance between maintaining speed and saving their tires. Restarts could also create opportunities to gain positions, while pit strategy may become a major factor if cautions change the complexion of the race.

The 150 lap distance leaves little room for costly mistakes, especially for drivers focused on advancing through the championship postseason.

With the championship battle continuing to develop, Friday night's race offers another opportunity for contenders to separate themselves from the field.

Riggs arrives after a major victory, while Honeycutt will be looking to respond. The combination of championship pressure, Phoenix's demanding layout and a competitive field sets up an important night for the Truck Series.

The green flag is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET Friday on FS2 .

articles.title: Brewers Take Commanding 3-0 NLCS Lead With 6-2 Win Over Dodgers
articles.summary: Milwaukee Delivers Late Inning Knockout The Milwaukee Brewers moved one win away from the World Series on Wednesday night, defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers moved one win away from the World Series on Wednesday night, defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium.

Milwaukee used timely home runs and another strong pitching performance to take a commanding 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. The victory puts the Brewers on the verge of their first World Series appearance since 1982, while the defending champion Dodgers now face elimination.

Milwaukee wasted little time making its presence felt. Jackson Chourio opened the game with a leadoff home run against Dodgers starter Blake Snell, giving the Brewers an early 1-0 advantage.

That lead held through the first five innings thanks to an impressive performance from rookie left-hander Robert Gasser. The young pitcher allowed just three hits across five scoreless innings, keeping Los Angeles' dangerous lineup off the scoreboard.

Gasser's outing gave Milwaukee's offense time to build momentum and put pressure on the Dodgers, who entered the game needing a victory to get back into the series.

Los Angeles finally broke through in the sixth inning. Will Smith delivered a two-run double that brought home Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, giving the Dodgers a 2-1 lead and briefly energizing the home crowd.

However, Milwaukee responded immediately in the following inning.

Jake Bauers launched a two-run home run to put the Brewers back in front, and Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo shot. The back-to-back homers transformed a one-run deficit into a 4-2 Milwaukee advantage and silenced the Dodger Stadium crowd.

The Brewers added another run in the eighth inning when Brice Turang scored on a wild pitch, extending the lead to 5-2.

Milwaukee added one more run in the ninth to complete the scoring and secure the four-run victory.

While the home runs grabbed the headlines, Milwaukee's pitching was equally important.

Gasser set the tone early, and the bullpen handled the remaining innings to protect the lead. The Dodgers finished with just five hits, struggling to generate consistent offense against the Brewers' pitching staff.

Shohei Ohtani also continued to have a difficult postseason at the plate, adding to Los Angeles' offensive concerns.

The victory gives Milwaukee a 3-0 series advantage, leaving Los Angeles with no margin for error.

The Brewers have received contributions from their pitching staff and lineup throughout the series, while the Dodgers have struggled to find the consistency needed to defend their championship.

Milwaukee now needs just one more victory to reach the World Series. Los Angeles must win four straight games to keep its season alive.

After another impressive performance, the Brewers are firmly in control of the NLCS and closing in on a historic opportunity.

articles.title: Teremoana Teremoana vs Hemi Ahio headlines November 18th Matchroom show in Melbourne
articles.summary: Teremoana Teremoana will squeeze in a fourth fight and second main event of 2026 against Hemi Ahio
articles.body:
Paris Olympian turned slow-walked heavyweight prospect Teremoana Teremoana is set for his second straight Matchroom main event, this time battling Tonga's Hemi Ahio on November 18th at Pullman Melbourne Albert Park.

Despite falling in the 2024 quarterfinals to eventual gold medalist Bakhodir Jalolov, Teremoana (12-0, 12 KO), who'd previously dipped his toes in the pro scene, looked to be the most promising big man to emerge from the games. He's been plenty busy, but that's about all you can say about his tenure in the paid ranks; nobody's taken him past the second round because Matchroom's made no effort to pit him against someone who can take him past the second round. His record is littered with professional victims like Curtis Harper, Bowie Tupou, and most recently DeAndre Savage, who boasted one win over an opponent with a >.500 record and lasted all of 86 seconds into the second round.

"I'm excited to be fighting again down in Melbourne and this time headlining against a strong opponent from New Zealand in Hemi Ahio," said Teremoana.

"I am really looking forward to the challenge he will bring. Nothing changes for me. I am here to prove I am the best and Ahio is the next obstacle in my way. I respect what he's achieved but he shouldn't have taken this fight.

"I've been training hard and with another five weeks of preparation until fight night I plan to show the difference in levels. God willing, I will be victorious."

Ahio (25-1, 19 KO) followed a similar blueprint as Teremoana minus the pedigree, feasting on the dregs of Australia's and New Zealand's heavyweight scenes for nearly a decade. He even fought the incredibly large but very bad Julius Long twice, only to bite off more than he could chew against Lucas Browne victim Faiga Opelu and suffer a stoppage loss in 2022. His six fights since have been garbage, including a TKO of 0-3 Richie Feulufai, a TKO of an even more cooked Browne, a split decision over Opelu in their rematch, and a knockout of 3-5 Joe Ageli in his last fight.

13 years in the ring and nothing to show for it. Still, he clears the unbelievably low bar Teremoana has set. Maybe he'll be good enough for Teremoana to actually learn something.

"I'm in great shape, maybe in the best shape I have been my entire career," said Ahio, who has lost just once in 26 contests with 25 wins on his resumé, including 19 stoppages.

"There's going to be fireworks, and we will both be dropping big bombs. I'm ready to throw down with the big man. Let's go!"

The best fight on the card is actually the co-feature, which sees undefeated middleweight Mitch Leek (14-0, 8 KO) fight never-before-stopped veteran Joel Camilleri (31-8-1, 15 KO). Not much else of interest to those who aren't Oceania diehards, but they did screw up the formatting on their press release and accidentally cut out the last bit, which I thought was funny.

articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks fell short against the New Orleans Pelicans, 101-97 , in the preseason at American Airlines Center on Wednesday, dropping to 1-2.

But it should not be a cause for concern for the Mavericks, who are entering the upcoming season with optimism, fueled by the continued ascent of Cooper Flagg in his second year and the much-awaited return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury.

The Mavericks are also high on Zaccharie Risacher , whom they acquired in a three-team trade with the Atlanta Hawks and the Oklahoma City Thunder in July.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

After the game against the Pelicans, coach Dusty May highlighted Risacher's attributes, touting the different ways the 21-year-old wingman can contribute.

"The things that he's been able to hang his hat on consistently: The offensive rebounding piece and running the lanes in transition," said May in the video posted by The Smoking Cuban's Noah Weber.

"Him as an off-ball cutter. He made open shots. He just looked extremely comfortable. Just picking his spots, understanding who's on the floor each and every possession. He's someone who can impact the game in a lot of ways."

Risacher had six points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals, and one block in 23 minutes. He, however, only shot 3-of-11 from the field, including 0-of-7 from long distance.

Risacher has yet to live up to being the No. 1 pick in 2024. The change of scenery with the Mavericks could help him unlock his untapped potential.

While there is still plenty of room for improvement, May's vote of confidence should go a long way for Risacher.

articles.body: Roman Reigns has been credited as one of the greatest WWE superstars of his generation. He broke into the business with a rich lineage behind him, coming from the illustrious Anoa’i family that has produced legends like The Rock, Wild Samoans, Rikishi, Yokozuna, and more. Recently, Reigns was asked about nepotism prevalent in wrestling, and he pointed out an interesting fact.Roman Reigns said past generations did not allow outsiders to enter the wrestling businessIn an interview with Club Shay Shay, Roman Reigns was asked if nepotism paved the way for a kickstart in the business. He admitted that, but said it wasn't the case decades ago. Reigns said,“I mean, we do have the advantage, but if you told me 20 years ago to 40 years ago, we definitely had the advantage because we know about Fight Club. Nobody knew about Fight Club back then. There was a mystique around the business.”However, the OTC revealed that past generational wrestlers kept outsiders out to protect the business. He added that today it's different and much easier.”If you tried to get in, they beat you up for real. They don’t want everybody in the business. They don’t want to share our secrets. Right now, all you got to do is like go on Instagram. Follow WWE. You can get a tryout tomorrow. So it’s just a little bit different nowadays”, said Reigns.Roman Reigns will compete at WWE Crown Jewel 2026Roman Reigns has been the reigning World Heavyweight Champion since dethroning CM Punk at WrestleMania 42. Following his victory, Reigns was announced to compete in a marquee bout at WWE’s upcoming Premium Live Event, Crown Jewel 2026.The OTC will square off against Sami Zayn, who is the reigning Undisputed WWE Champion on SmackDown.
